answer: A sybil tax stops bulk fake identities by making each one pay a sunk cost. To join, each agent pays twice its 30-day reward, logged as a ferrous record. The kernel of the check: auditors sample identities each epoch and revoke untraced payments. Making 1,000 fakes costs 1,000 fees, about 60,000 credits, while an honest agent pays once and keeps undiluted rewards. Pooling fees in one lagoon does not help, since the tax is per identity.
